title: Training Note: Coverage Lapses and the Loyalty Credit of a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy Vehicle Addition
content:
On a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy, the loyalty credit carried into a vehicle addition charge is taken in a continuous-coverage share. That share follows the lapse marker on the policy record.

## The rule

| Lapse marker on the policy record | Continuous-coverage share of the loyalty credit |
|---|---|
| None | One: the whole credit |
| Dated 36 months or more before the day the charge is booked | Half (0.5) of the credit |
| Dated less than 36 months before the day the charge is booked | Nil: none of the credit |

## Questions answered

**What is a lapse marker?**
A cancellation effective date kept on a reinstated policy marks a lapse in coverage. A policy record carrying no cancellation effective date has no lapse marker.

**From which day is the age of the marker measured?**
From the marker's date to the day the charge is booked. A marker dated exactly 36 months before that day falls in the half-credit line. One dated 35 months before falls in the none line.

**Hypothetical: a vehicle addition booked on a policy whose lapse marker is dated four years before booking. What part of the loyalty credit is taken?**
Half of it: four years is 48 months, at least 36.

**Hypothetical: the same policy with a lapse marker dated one year before booking?**
None of it: 12 months is less than 36.

**Hypothetical: no lapse marker at all?**
The whole of it.
